exposure: Labor induction protocols (country-specific practices in Poland vs. Germany)
outcome: Duration of preinduction cervical ripening and induction
Postpartum complications (perineal tears, episiotomies, anemia, cervical tears, revision of the uterine cavity)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 304 pregnant women (154 in Poland, 150 in Germany) with postdate pregnancy, an unfavorable cervix (Bishop score < 6), or other indications for induction, who underwent preinduction cervical ripening and labor induction, excluding those who had undergone cesarean section.
finding: The study found that cervical ripening (Bishop Score change) was more effective in Germany, and German neonates had a significantly higher proportion of normal umbilical cord pH, while specific maternal postpartum complications varied by country.
mod_finding: Postpartum complications related to the mode of birth, such as cervical tears, uterine cavity revision, and episiotomy, were more common in Poland, while first- and second-degree perineal tears were more frequent in Germany.
